title: How Middle Powers Can Survive the AI Race
gist: Carnegie researchers frame middle-power AI strategy on two axes: the speed of frontier progress and the 'frontier premium' gap between leading and cheap/open models, yielding four scenarios (Chokepoint World, Transform or Die, Adopt for Advantage, Tiered Access). They argue supply-chain chokepoint leverage and adoption capacity are robust across scenarios, while from-scratch sovereign frontier models (costing up to $900 billion) are a poor bet.

insights.claim: In 'Chokepoint World' (fast progress, large gap), labs block distillation and secure their insights, the U.S. keeps its chip lead via export controls, and access to the best systems is sharply restricted, dividing the world into AI haves and have-nots.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Phillips-Robins
insights.so_what: In this world frontier-lab moats and chip export controls are most valuable; middle powers without leverage lose access.

insights.claim: In 'Transform or Die' (fast progress, small gap), AI developers may struggle to capture returns as profits are competed away, with value shifting to compute providers turning energy into tokens and businesses converting tokens into economic value.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Phillips-Robins
insights.so_what: A small frontier gap is bearish for model-developer margins and bullish for compute, energy, and AI adopters.

insights.claim: In 'Adopt for Advantage' (slow progress, small gap), AI company valuations might collapse if investors decide transformative results will take longer, and frontier developers would likely operate on thin margins while gains flow to finance, consumer tech, and AI integrators in law and healthcare.

insights.claim: In 'Tiered Access' (slow progress, large gap), progress plateaus but a few leaders keep a durable edge through talent concentration, implementation data, or compute costs, and both frontier developers and skilled AI users capture value.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Phillips-Robins
insights.so_what: Durable moats with slower progress favor incumbents and services firms over moonshot challengers.

insights.claim: Indicators to watch: continued effective distillation points to a small-gap world, strong unit economics at top firms suggest a large gap, and labs reporting diminishing returns on new training runs would suggest slowing progress.

insights.claim: Building leverage at supply-chain chokepoints or scarce resources is valuable in almost every scenario and most valuable where middle powers have the most to lose.
